title: Features, Labels and Baseline Models
learning_objectives: Describe a dataset as a feature matrix X and a label vector y
Write models as classes with fit and predict methods
Build mean and majority-class baselines and explain why every model needs one
entry_point: class MeanRegressor; class MajorityClassifier; mse(y_true, y_pred); accuracy(y_true, y_pred)
hints: Before fitting, the attribute does not exist: check `hasattr(self, "mean_")` in `predict`.
`labels, counts = np.unique(y, return_counts=True)`; `np.unique` sorts labels, so `labels[np.argmax(counts)]` picks the smallest on ties.
`np.full(len(X), self.mean_)` repeats a value; MSE is `np.mean((y_true - y_pred) ** 2)`.

failure_feedback.advice: Store the training mean in `self.mean_` and repeat it once per row of X.
Raise ValueError in `predict` if the model has not been fitted.
Use `np.unique(..., return_counts=True)` and `np.argmax`, which picks the first (smallest) label on ties.
Check that lengths match and are non-zero before computing.
